title: Restriction cocycle for compact support on strict coefficient systems
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, schemes $X,Y$, and a factorization $f=pj$ with $j:X\hookrightarrow\overline X$ open and $p:\overline X\to Y$ proper [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. Let $R_\bullet\xrightarrow{i}S_\bullet\xrightarrow{h}T_\bullet$ be compatible maps of inverse sequences of finite commutative rings annihilated by powers of $\ell$. On the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] use strict semilinear module systems: an object has $R_n$-module sheaves $L_n$ and $R_{n+1}$-linear transitions $L_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_{R_{n+1}\to R_n}L_n$. Equivalently these are module sheaves for the ring sheaf $R_\bullet$ on the diagram site, and likewise for $S,T$ [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization]. Use their ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $H_R=Rp_{*,R}j_{!,R}$, where open extension acts termwise and $Rp_{*,R}$ is total derived system direct image, and similarly $H_S,H_T$. Restriction $U_i^W$ acts termwise on systems and exactly on derived categories [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Let $\rho_W:U_i^WU_h^W\cong U_{hi}^W$ be the identification with identical underlying sheaves and scalar action $r x=h(i(r))x$.

There are specified natural isomorphisms $d_i:H_RU_i^X\cong U_i^YH_S$ (and $d_h,d_{hi}$). The open part is the section-preserving identity on the open and zero off it. The proper part is normalized by K-injective comparison: if $J$ is K-injective over the target coefficient diagram and $u:U_iJ\to I$ is a K-injective resolution over the source diagram, its component is $[p_*u]^{-1}$ under the derived evaluation identifications. This specifies the entire derived-system transformation, not only its finite evaluations, and does not require $U_iJ$ itself to be K-injective. Then
$$d_{hi,L}\circ H_R(\rho_{X,L})=\rho_{Y,H_TL}\circ U_i^Y(d_{h,L})\circ d_{i,U_h^XL}$$
for every $L$ in the derived category of $T_\bullet$-systems. The comparison for the identity ring-sequence map is identity under the canonical unit identifications. The finite evaluations are the usual open/proper restriction comparisons of [lem-sf-direct-image-scalar-restriction-cocycle, lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]. These assertions are equalities in the derived categories of entire strict systems, before evaluation or realization. They require neither flat coefficient maps, bounded objects, nor any assumption that evaluations are faithful on derived morphisms.

proof.text:
form the varying-ring vertical sequence sites. Module-sheaf restriction is exact,
so localize its identity-on-sections composition and unit maps. For proper direct image,
the two factorizations of the same ringed diagram-topos morphism give a comparison by
unbounded derived pushforward composition. On a target-coefficient K-injective H and a
source-coefficient K-injective resolution v of its restriction, this is the inverse of
[p_*v] after the displayed quotient and exact-restriction identifications; restriction
need not preserve K-injectives. Normalized derived-comparison composition gives the
proper cocycle. For open extension, restriction preserves the presheaf formula, the
original module on the open and zero off it, together with all transitions. Abelian
sheafification and exact localization give its normalized comparison and cocycle. Paste
the open comparison with the proper comparison. Naturality of the latter moves the
second open comparison through it; the proper and open cocycles then give the displayed
compact-support cocycle. For identity coefficient maps the resolution can be identity
on K-injectives, giving the unit there, and naturality transports it to every derived
object. Finally the inverse proper comparison is the mate of the inverse-image square:
on K-injective representatives the triangle identity identifies this mate with [p_*v].
Evaluation preserves the specified units, counits and inverse-image squares, so that mate
evaluates to the finite normalized comparison. The same section identity handles the
open part. No equality of system morphisms is deduced from equality after evaluation.

Apply the open and proper factor coherence theorems to this same c, obtaining normalized geometric squares, open comparisons o, and proper comparisons q. Form Comparison from these four actual records. Its iso is the specified paste P_B(o_a) followed by q_a.

For composition, expand Comparison.iso. Apply P_B to the open cocycle, and then apply the proper cocycle at J_D L. Naturality of q_a along o_b moves P_B(U_a(o_b)) across q_a. Associativity and functoriality give exactly the compact-support equation. For the unit, expand the same paste, use the proper unit at J_B L, combine the two P_B images, and use the open unit. These are equations on entire derived systems.

Apply finite normalization to each constructed Comparison. Its theorem applies to every datum with the original section, open-unit and proper-resolution normalizations, and supplies precisely Nonempty(FiniteCompatibility d).

lean.statement:
theorem compactSupportRestrictionCocycle (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime]
    {X Z Y : Scheme.{u}} (j : X ⟶ Z) [IsOpenImmersion j] (p : Z ⟶ Y) [IsProper p] :
    ∃ c : RestrictionIdentifications.{u} l,
      ∃ d : ∀ (B C : Etale.SystemProjection.Coefficients.{u} l)
        (a : B.rings ⟶ C.rings), Comparison a j p,
        (∀ (B C D : Etale.SystemProjection.Coefficients.{u} l)
          (a : B.rings ⟶ C.rings) (b : C.rings ⟶ D.rings)
          (L : VaryingRing.Derived (levels D) (steps D) X),
          (support B j p).map ((c.rho X a b).hom.app L) ≫
              (d B D (a ≫ b)).iso.hom.app L =
            (d B C a).iso.hom.app ((derivedRestriction X b).obj L) ≫
              (derivedRestriction Y a).map ((d C D b).iso.hom.app L) ≫
              (c.rho Y a b).hom.app ((support D j p).obj L)) ∧
        (∀ (B : Etale.SystemProjection.Coefficients.{u} l)
          (L : VaryingRing.Derived (levels B) (steps B) X),
          (d B B (𝟙 B.rings)).iso.hom.app L ≫
              (c.derivedUnit Y B).hom.app ((support B j p).obj L) =
            (support B j p).map ((c.derivedUnit X B).hom.app L)) ∧
        (∀ (B C : Etale.SystemProjection.Coefficients.{u} l)
          (a : B.rings ⟶ C.rings), Nonempty (FiniteCompatibility (d B C a)))
